label: alg:markov-trace
title: Markov trace on the Iwahori–Hecke algebra $H_n(q)$
html:
Algorithm (Markov trace on H_n(q)). Compute the categorical observation \mathrm{tr}_M\colon H_n(q) \to R[q, q^{-1}] of a braid word w \in B_n in Hecke normal form.

Input

  • Braid word w = \sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k} in B_n (the closure of w is the knot or link whose mass we predict).
  • Substrate parameter q \in R — either symbolic (for an algebraic identity) or pinned to q_0 for a numerical evaluation.

Output

  • The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(w)) \in R[q, q^{-1}] as a Laurent polynomial (symbolic mode) or as an arbitrary-precision scalar evaluation at q = q_0 (numerical mode).

Algorithm

1. Reduce w to its Hecke normal form NF(w) via the
   Gröbner–Shirshov rewriter (Algorithm 2).
2. Decompose NF(w) along the Wedderburn isotypic components
   H_n(q) ≅ ⊕_{λ ⊢ n} M_{d_λ}(R) (Algorithm 5).
3. For each partition λ ⊢ n with multiplicity y_λ(q), evaluate the
   irreducible character χ^λ(σ_w) on the Hoefsmit representation.
4. Return the Frobenius pairing tr_M(σ_w) = Σ_λ y_λ(q) · χ^λ(σ_w).

Correctness conditions

Correctness follows from three upstream results.

  1. Existence and uniqueness of the trace is established by the axiomatic closed form (prop:markov-trace-axiomatic-closed-form): \mathrm{tr}_M is the unique R-linear functional on H_n(q) satisfying (i) cyclicity, (ii) the Markov axiom \mathrm{tr}_M(a\sigma_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(a) for a \in H_n(q), and (iii) normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1.
  2. The recursive-reducer formula (prop:markov-trace-recursive-reducer) gives a terminating reduction strategy by descent on braid index, so step 1 always terminates.
  3. The Frobenius pairing in step 4 is justified by the Wedderburn decomposition; cyclicity makes the trace partition-respecting, so the sum is well-defined and independent of the chosen representative within each conjugacy class.

Complexity

Polynomial in the braid index n and the word length |w| in the symbolic regime. The dominant cost is the GS reduction in step 1 (worst case exponential in n, polynomial in |w| after caching cycle-equivalent words). The Wedderburn sum in step 4 has |\{\lambda \vdash n\}| terms — for nucleon-scale knots (n \leq 9) the partition count is at most 30.

Python API entry point

from qou_mass import compute_tr_M, canonical_braid

word = canonical_braid(Z=1, N=0)              # proton braid 𝓑₃
trM  = compute_tr_M(Z=1, N=0)                 # Decimal at q = q_0

The lower-level pyhecke surface exposes the trace on a Hecke normal form: pyhecke.nf_tr(nf). The compile-time Markov-trace vector for the 6-element basis is the constant pyhecke.TR_M. The PyO3 binding pyhecke_native calls the Rust core directly.

Witness contract

Canonical witness: markov-free-energy-qvalues.witness.json. Per-particle assembly traces are emitted separately as markov-trace-assembly-{proton,neutron,deuteron}.derivation.json. Each witness records the input braid word, the chosen q evaluation, the resulting Laurent polynomial (symbolic mode) or mpmath scalar (numerical mode, default 65 dps compute / 50 dps serialisation), and a SHA-256 digest of the canonical script source for reproducibility.

Notes

Precision regime: the symbolic mode is exact (L1 met trivially). The numerical mode at q = q_0 meets L1 to 10^{-50} by the precision discipline of qou-substrate. The per-observable L2 target inherits the calibration floor of the downstream nucleon mass ratio (step 9a).

Edge cases: the identity braid 1 \in B_n has \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1; closure of any braid containing a full twist \Delta_n^2 in the centre acquires a factor (q^{n(n-1)}) from the central character (Schur–Weyl).

*For large-A scaling (Step 9b atom braids), the multi-nucleon braid word features a monotone non-decreasing generator sequence. Nucleon k uses \sigma_{3k}, \sigma_{3k+1} and one interface crossing \sigma_{3k+2}, never revisiting a generator. Thus, each O_g is a polynomial in a single \sigma_g.

In the multiplicity-free seminormal (Gelfand–Zetlin) basis, \sigma_g moves exactly one level of the chain \varnothing \subset s_1 \subset \cdots \subset s_n = \lambda. Trace closure forces each O_g into its diagonal block. This collapses Steps 3–4 into a transfer matrix over fine-Bratteli edges s_g \subset s_{g+1}. We compute every \chi^\lambda(\beta) in a single sweep without materializing the d_\lambda-dimensional Hoefsmit representation. The computational cost scales with the fine-Bratteli edge count (e.g., a few thousand at n = 21) rather than n!. This extends numerical \mathrm{tr}_M evaluation at q_0 to A \geq 6 (^6Li, ^7Li, and beyond) in seconds.

The implementation resides in chi_monotone_transfer.py, with per-atom trace assembly in tr_m_atom_via_transfer.py (witness tr-m-atom-via-transfer.witness.json). We validate it to the 50-dps floor against Hoefsmit characters (n \leq 6) and cached per-basis-vector trace witnesses (n \leq 12). The production binding consumers binding_canonical and canonical_tr_m_via_branching (A \geq 3) route their atom-trace through this transfer path. The brute-force atom-level Wedderburn tower (atom_level_wedderburn_tower.py) serves strictly as a d_\lambda-explicit cross-check.*
